evidence_kind: Additive direct-processor hidden-state witness; not a replacement native-wrapper or audio-partition gate
trigger: An already-active sixteen-voice extension must receive the final program after an active VST3 supported-curve block recalls Legacy and then modern again, even though the first recall cancels all trajectories.
fixture: Use normal JUCE MIDI and the real HostAutomationBlock tagged as VST3. Warm sixteen notes, attach all eighteen supported queues, then send Legacy program 0 followed by curated program 0 in one uninterrupted 1024-frame block. Inspect through the pre-existing PresetSaveAccess friend; no production instrumentation is added.
required: The warmup reaches both engines and activates the existing extension
The final program identity and policy are independently fixed by bank 0 program 0
APVTS and both active engines exactly equal the final program's physical values, as independently prepared through ordinary public preset recall
Each supported queue is published once, before preset writes, and remains cancelled through later recalls and wrapper-scope exit
The extension remains active through the recalled block and wrapper-scope exit, and retires only at the next ordinary block boundary because the final program selects eight voices
Tagged empty-queue and untagged ordinary no-queue paths remain byte-identical in PCM and state; their historical secondary-engine state is characterized rather than corrected
All original native fixtures and acceptance limits remain unchanged
limits: No split-after-recall audio oracle is used because the original extension lifetime is block-boundary dependent. This fixture requires no new native AU behavior and grants no native macOS, DAW, UI, real-time or release qualification.
